title: Provider-neutral harness seam and the dsh adapter
summary: Introduces a provider-neutral `harness` module — a `Harness` trait, a `CommandRunner` seam with a real process runner, plain-data `HarnessResult`/`HarnessCapabilities`, and in-memory fakes — plus the first concrete adapter, `DshHarness`, which runs `dsh --profile headless --json -`, parses its newline-delimited JSON events, guards the repository with git status/head/branch probes, and reports capabilities by probing `--version`, `--help` and `--dump-config`. A new `job-blocked` journal payload carries a clarification question out of a run.

lanes.label: Factory core
lanes.subtitle: osf crate
lanes.summary: The existing factory modules the new seam plugs into: the journal that records events and the reviewer environment allow-list.

lanes.label: Harness seam
lanes.subtitle: provider-neutral
lanes.summary: The new `harness` module: traits, plain data, the real process runner, and the in-memory fakes. Names no harness and no vendor.

lanes.label: Adapters
lanes.subtitle: concrete harnesses
lanes.summary: Concrete implementations of the seam. This change adds the `dsh` adapter.

lanes.label: External processes
lanes.subtitle: spawned by the runner
lanes.summary: The child processes the runner starts: the agent binary and git.

nodes.label: Journal
nodes.subtitle: Payload / replay
nodes.summary: Append-only event log. Gains a `JobBlocked` payload so a run that ended by asking a question is recorded with its cause and question text.

nodes.label: Reviewer env allow-list
nodes.subtitle: RUN_ENV_VARS
nodes.summary: The list of environment names a reviewer process may inherit. Widened from private to `pub(crate)` so the dsh adapter can reuse it as the git allow-list.

nodes.label: Harness trait
nodes.subtitle: run / capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and an external coding harness: one `run` and one `capabilities` method, both taking a `CommandRunner`. Object-safe.

nodes.label: Harness data types
nodes.subtitle: Task, Result, Usage, Capability
nodes.summary: Plain serializable data: `HarnessTask`, `Actor`, `Usage`, `HarnessOutcome`, `HarnessResult`, `Capability`, `HarnessCapabilities`, `HarnessError`. `HarnessResult::blocked_event` turns an asked outcome into a journal payload.

nodes.label: Prompt contract
nodes.subtitle: build_prompt / question_line
nodes.summary: Builds the task prompt with the four rules appended, and reads a trailing `QUESTION:` line out of a final message as the question signal.

nodes.label: RealCommandRunner
nodes.subtitle: child process + timeout
nodes.summary: Runs a `CommandSpec` as a real child: clears the environment, sets exactly the spec's, drains both pipes on threads, feeds stdin, and kills the whole process tree at the deadline.

nodes.label: FakeRunner
nodes.subtitle: scripted CommandRunner
nodes.summary: In-memory `CommandRunner` that replays scripted outputs and records every command, so adapter tests start no process.

nodes.label: FakeHarness
nodes.subtitle: scripted Harness
nodes.summary: In-memory `Harness` that replays scripted results and records every task, for engine tests that need no adapter.

nodes.label: DshHarness
nodes.subtitle: Harness impl
nodes.summary: The first concrete adapter. Validates the task, guards the repository with git, runs `dsh --profile headless --json -`, parses events, checks the head did not move, and reports capabilities by probing the binary.

nodes.label: Event parser
nodes.subtitle: parse_events / parse_changed_files
nodes.summary: Pure functions over the adapter's inputs: newline-delimited JSON events to session id, final message, summed usage and first turn failure; NUL-separated porcelain to sorted changed paths; version and help text to capability answers.

nodes.label: DshConfig
nodes.subtitle: program, env, pinned version
nodes.summary: How to reach the binary: its program, its complete child environment, and the pinned version `--version` must report.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: headless profile
nodes.summary: The external coding agent. Reads the prompt on stdin, prints newline-delimited JSON events on stdout, and reports no model name and no cost figure.

nodes.label: git
nodes.subtitle: status / rev-parse
nodes.summary: The repository tool the adapter shells out to for the clean-tree guard, the head commit and the branch. Runs with only PATH, HOME and GIT_* names.

nodes.label: Harness fixtures
nodes.subtitle: recorded dsh runs
nodes.summary: Recorded `dsh` output: a created-file run, a question run, prose-question runs, a missing-credential run, the version, the headless help and a profile dump.

nodes.label: Harness tests
nodes.subtitle: fake run + neutrality
nodes.summary: End-to-end runs through the fakes, capability reports, and a scanner that fails if the provider-neutral folder names an agent or a model vendor.

edges.label: implements
edges.summary: The adapter is the first implementation of the seam; everything it returns is the seam's plain data.
The adapter builds the prompt with the rules and reads the trailing `QUESTION:` line.
The adapter delegates all parsing to the pure functions.
The adapter is constructed from a `DshConfig`.
The adapter never starts a process itself; it hands `CommandSpec`s to the runner it is given.
An asked outcome becomes a `JobBlocked` payload through `HarnessResult::blocked_event`.
The git environment allow-list reuses the reviewer allow-list.

edges.label: --profile headless --json -
edges.summary: The runner starts `dsh` with the prompt on stdin and reads newline-delimited JSON events from stdout.

edges.label: status / rev-parse
edges.summary: The runner starts git for the clean-tree guard, the head commit and the branch, with the minimal environment.

edges.label: same trait
edges.summary: The fake and the real runner implement the same `CommandRunner` trait, so adapter tests exercise the same code path.

edges.label: same trait
edges.summary: The fake harness implements the same `Harness` trait, so engine tests can swap it for the adapter.
The integration tests drive the adapter through the fakes and assert the exact commands that reach the runner.
The tests include the recorded runs, version, help and dump as compile-time fixtures.

edges.label: neutrality scan
edges.summary: A test scans the provider-neutral folder and fails if it names an agent or a model vendor.
